quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When should you use high beam headlights at night?

options.text: When you are following another vehicle.
When you meet an oncoming vehicle.
When driving in open country with few other vehicles.
When driving in fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving in open country with few other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Use high beams in open country where few other vehicles are present. Dim your lights when following a vehicle, meeting oncoming traffic, or driving in fog.

questions.question: What should you adjust first when you get in a car to drive?

options.text: Your seat belt.
The steering wheel.
Your rearview mirror.
Your seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat.
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat first so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel once your seat is in the right position.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
It means you can turn in the direction of the arrow.
It means a green arrow will appear next.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow has the same meaning as a yellow traffic light. Slow down and prepare to stop for a red light.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
No U-turns.
No exit.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: You are backing out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Sound your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check if the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check if the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out and walk around your car to check behind it before backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially when children are nearby.

questions.question: What is used on some highways to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights.
Flashing yellow lights.
White lines on the side of the road.
White arrows in the middle of the lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes.
questions.explanation: White arrows show which lanes to use for specific purposes, such as driving straight or turning.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time, which vehicle must yield?

options.text: Either one.
The vehicle on the left.
The vehicle on the right.
Neither.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left.
questions.explanation: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right when both enter the intersection at the same time.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if there is no traffic.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs indicate?

options.text: School zones.
No passing zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. The sign will also have text to confirm it is a no passing area.

questions.question: What color are signs for areas of public recreation?

options.text: Orange.
Red.
Green.
Brown.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown.
questions.explanation: Brown signs show areas for public recreation or of historical importance. They help you find places when traveling.

questions.question: A single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A dashed line means drivers can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:

options.text: Loss of hearing.
Pollution.
Carbon monoxide poisoning.
Poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful fumes from your vehicle. A leak allows carbon monoxide to enter the passenger area. Fix any leaks right away.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you must:

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Slow down without stopping completely.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely. Look for pedestrians and crossing traffic. Wait until the intersection is clear before driving.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, it is usually best to:

options.text: Drive slowly while waiting for an opening.
Speed up faster than freeway traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to freeway traffic speed. This lets you blend in smoothly and safely. Merging traffic must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when stopping on:

options.text: A wet or icy road.
Paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Wet or icy roads increase your stopping distance. Loose gravel or stones also increase stopping distance.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep a constant speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Gradually speed up as you exit. Speeding up in a curve makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning drivers on a green light must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning drivers on a green light must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign is used with a traffic light. It tells drivers turning left that they do not have the right-of-way. Wait for oncoming traffic to pass before turning.

questions.question: A work zone:

options.text: Can be moving or stationary.
Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require drivers to slow down and pay attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be in one place or moving (like striping, mowing, or snow removal vehicles). They are marked with orange signs with black lettering. Slow down and pay attention in work zones.

questions.question: You should be cautious when passing a bicycle because:

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pulling out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.
questions.explanation: Always be careful when passing a bicycle. The cyclist may suddenly swerve to avoid something on the road. Always drive carefully around bicyclists.

questions.question: An approaching driver fails to dim their high beam headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This prevents the bright lights from blinding you and lets you see enough of the road to stay on course until the other vehicle passes.
